Contacts engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume contact-saving capability covers storefront language. Xcode, Developer portal, and Connect actually separate address-book behavior from product-page copy:

  • CNContactStore & ContactsUI — configured in your app to read, create, or update contacts. Controls whether Add to Contacts sheets appear. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Contact permission prompts — NSContactsUsageDescription strings in Info.plist and runtime permission dialogs. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains contact-saving value to buyers.
  • In-app contact forms & field labels — name, phone, email fields on your New contact screen. Your listing may mention save-to-address-book; implementing CNContact write logic is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Contacts framework flags in the binary.

Working Add to Contacts in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Add to Contacts-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Contact-saving listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe address-book features — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Add to Contacts vs generic "people" or "network"

US pages use "Add to Contacts", "Save contact", or "Build your network." Chinese buyers expect concise 添加到通讯录, 保存联系人, or 一键存入通讯录 phrasing rather than English slogans left on screenshot overlays — without implying you are the built-in Contacts app or a full CRM replacement.

Contact scope without address-book overreach

Description and caption lines should name the contact-saving flows your app actually supports — card scan import, lead capture, one-tap save from chat — without promising full device contact sync, unauthorized address-book reads, or CRM features your backend does not support. AppLocale rewrites from your English claims; we do not invent contact behavior.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need contact-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 通讯录, 联系人, and 保存联系人 each signal different intent from generic networking keywords.

Screenshot captions on contact-saving frames

Gallery frames that show Add to Contacts sheets, New contact forms, or address-book sync UI need one-line zh-Hans captions — "一键保存到通讯录" not "Add to Contacts" burned into the product page story.

Common mistakes on Add to Contacts zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming contact-saving localizes automatically — CNContactStore wired in Xcode; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and contact-saving screenshot caption lines still English
  • Calling the app "Contacts replacement" — 替代通讯录 overclaims when the app only saves new leads or imports cards
  • Implying full address-book access — listing claims read-all-contacts when the app only writes new entries with permission
  • Conflating listing copy with in-app contact field labels — CNContact givenName labels and New contact form placeholders are binary localization, not Connect metadata
  • English "Save contact" on zh-Hans screenshots — Connect caption fields are Chinese but burned-in contact mockups on PNG exports are still Latin
  • What's New still English after contact-saving launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when Add to Contacts shipped in a recent version
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement CNContactStore or ContactsUI — contact picker wiring and address-book write logic are outside listing rewrite
